name: io.github.Vortx-AI/emem
title: emem, the verifiable memory protocol for the physical world
description: Shared, verifiable memory for AI agents and robots: signed tokens that resolve and verify offline.

directoryCompliance.annotations: every tool emits title + annotations.{readOnlyHint,destructiveHint} on tools/list
directoryCompliance.toolListing: tools/list at the advertised /mcp returns a 15-tool core surface (~40 KB); /mcp/full returns all 105 (about a quarter megabyte). The split is listing-only: tools/call dispatches any of the 105 by name at either endpoint, and the emem_tools tool maps the full surface on demand. /mcp is advertised deliberately, so a host connecting cold from a directory spends 40 KB of context rather than 200 KB.
directoryCompliance.auth: No account, API key or OAuth token is required, and none is issued. Reads are unauthenticated and every stored memory is world-readable. Writes are unauthenticated but not anonymous: the MCP write surface (memory_create, memory_str_replace, memory_insert, memory_delete, memory_rename) and the REST attestation endpoints (POST /v1/attest, POST /v1/challenge) each require an ed25519 `attester` binding over a blake3 preimage of (verb, path, body_hash). Writes under /memories/by_attester/<pubkey8>/ are accepted only from the key whose shortcode matches; elsewhere the first attester to create a path owns it and only that key may change it; and a legacy record carrying no persisted attester is frozen, refused to every key including the operator's, because no key can prove ownership of it. Cross-key writes return 403 memory_namespace_violation.
directoryCompliance.dataHandling: Agent-written memory files persist and are world-readable by default. Entries written with kind: vault are AEAD-sealed against other callers, but the key derives from this responder's own ed25519 secret, so the operator can read vault plaintext; encrypt client-side if that matters. memory_delete unlinks the path from the index but the content-addressed blob and prior versions remain, because the write log is append-only and an issued receipt must stay verifiable. See https://emem.dev/privacy for what is stored, for how long, how to enumerate your own files, and how to request operator erasure.
directoryCompliance.originAllowlist: EMEM_ALLOWED_ORIGINS env var (comma-separated) flips CORS from `*` to a strict allowlist with Vary: Origin

environmentVariables.name: PORT
environmentVariables.description: PaaS port convention: the container entrypoint binds 0.0.0.0:$PORT when EMEM_BIND is not set explicitly. Falls back to 5051.

environmentVariables.name: EMEM_BIND
environmentVariables.description: Bind address for the HTTP server. When unset, the entrypoint derives it from PORT, falling back to 0.0.0.0:5051.

environmentVariables.name: EMEM_DATA
environmentVariables.description: Path to the persistent data directory (sled cache + ed25519 identity). Mount a volume here; on managed platforms that mount /data, set EMEM_DATA=/data.

environmentVariables.name: EMEM_PUBLIC_URL
environmentVariables.description: Optional canonical origin for self-referencing URLs in MCP responses (e.g. https://emem.dev). When unset the server falls back to urn:emem.

environmentVariables.name: EMEM_TLS_DOMAINS
environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated hostnames for built-in Let's Encrypt ACME (TLS-ALPN-01). When set, the server binds 0.0.0.0:443 instead of EMEM_BIND.
